transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes | Attendees: Alex Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Mark Ellis (Nova CTO), Jia Chen (Head of Integrations), Ravi Patel (SRE), Emily Soto (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick integration discovery to understand Nova's stack, latency/cost targets, preferred SDKs, and security needs. Discussed LangChain/LlamaIndex usage, gateway/proxy architecture, quotas/rate limits, and observability hooks. Next: send docs/pricing and schedule a benchmark POC.

00:00 Mark Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for the invite, Mark here from Nova Payments. We're evaluating options for hosted vs dedicated vs private for inference. Primary use case is fraud signal enrichment and customer support summarization.
00:18 Alex Morales: Great, Mark — thanks. Quick intro: I'm Alex, AE on this account, Priya and Liam are our SEs who will cover integration specifics. Can you give a sense of current stack?
00:30 Jia Chen: Sure — we run most services in GCP, Kubernetes GKE, use a mix of Python microservices and some nodejs lambda-style functions. We already use OpenAI for some prototypes but need more control on latency and cost at scale.
00:45 Priya Shah: Got it. Do you have expected QPS and tail-latency SLOs for the enrichment path? That determines whether hosted is enough or you need dedicated/private.
00:56 Emily Soto: For enrichment, peak is ~150 req/s, average ~40 req/s. Tail latency target p95 < 200ms for the enrichment API. For support summarization it's lower priority, p95 < 1s.
01:12 Liam O'Connor: Okay 150 qps peak — with hosted we can usually get good throughput but dedicated reserved GPU pools give more predictable tail latency. Private (VPC/on-prem) can help if you need strict data residency or very low variance.
01:28 Ravi Patel: Data residency is not primary, but we have PCI constraints and want audit logs and KMS integration for PII keys. We'll likely need a private control plane or dedicated with encrypted at-rest and KMS.
01:41 Priya Shah: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs for dedicated/private. For hosted we offer encryption-in-transit and per-tenant logs but dedicated is the typical path for PCI workloads.
01:55 Mark Ellis: Integration-wise, our infra team likes SDKs we can drop into services. Which SDKs do you support, and any examples with LangChain or LlamaIndex?
02:06 Priya Shah: We have first-class Python and Node SDKs, and we've published examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. I'll share a demo repo that shows a LangChain chain using Redwood's streaming responses and how to persist and reuse KV cache. It covers both sync and async patterns.
02:22 Jia Chen: Do you support the OpenAI-compatible API surface? We use a lot of OpenAI client code.
02:30 Liam O'Connor: Yes, the hosted API is mostly OpenAI-compatible for text and embedding calls. For advanced features we also offer Redwood-specific params (like routing policy hints, quantization profile hints). For dedicated/private you get the same SDK interface; endpoint differences are mostly host and auth.
02:50 Emily Soto: On the gateway/proxy side — we currently run an internal API gateway with rate limiting and tracing. Do customers run Redwood behind their gateway or use your edge gateway?
03:02 Alex Morales: Both patterns are supported. Many customers put Redwood behind their gateway/proxy to centralize rate limits and auth. Others use Redwood's gateway for token-level cost visibility and per-route metrics. If you need strict egress control, private deployments can sit inside your VPC so traffic doesn't cross public internet.
03:21 Ravi Patel: For rate limits, we need per-customer quotas, burst control, and graceful error behavior (429 vs queued). How configurable is that?
03:30 Priya Shah: We support per-api-key quotas, per-route throttles, and configurable burst tokens. There's also automatic fallback policies — if a dedicated pool is saturated, the router can failover to a cheaper variant or to hosted (if policy allows). We can expose 429s or have a queue with timeouts.
03:50 Mark Ellis: Observability: what hooks do you provide? We need token-level cost breakdown per request and distributed tracing that ties to our trace IDs.
04:00 Liam O'Connor: We provide per-request metrics (tokens, latency), streaming logs, and an ingestion path for OpenTelemetry traces. You can push your trace ID in headers and our traces will include the same correlation ID. Console shows per-route/model dashboards and cost breakdowns.
04:17 Emily Soto: Nice. Can we export raw events for internal analytics?
04:22 Priya Shah: Yes — event export to BigQuery/S3 or streaming via Kafka is supported for dedicated/private. Hosted customers can request a retention add-on or push logs to their storage depending on plan.
04:33 Jia Chen: About LangChain/LlamaIndex: does Redwood handle chunking/embeddings lifecycle or do teams manage that themselves? We want guidance because current code has duplication.
04:44 Priya Shah: We offer embedding endpoints and recommend using our SDK helpers for chunking and caching embeddings. Also we have a sample LlamaIndex connector in the repo that manages indexing and incremental updates — it's opinionated but meant to be a starting point.
05:02 Mark Ellis: On latency — 150 qps with p95 <200ms — would a dedicated pool of A10s be enough or do we need A100s?
05:12 Liam O'Connor: It depends on model size and sequence length; for smaller open models, A10/A30 with quantized weights can hit your targets if you optimize batching and cache prefixes. For larger Llama2-70B-style models you'd need heavier hardware. We'll size in the POC.
05:30 Ravi Patel: Security checklist — we need SSO, RBAC, audit logs, SOC2, and controls for export of data. Do you provide a security pack?
05:40 Alex Morales: Yes, we'll include SOC2 report, ISO summary, SSO/SAML setup docs, RBAC controls guide, and our data retention/exports policy in the package I'll send. For private deployments there's a full on-prem package with no external data egress.
05:55 Jia Chen: Any built-in protections for prompt injection or content scanning?
06:02 Priya Shah: We offer a content moderation pipeline option (hosted) and customers can plug in their own filters in the gateway layer. For private you can run the same moderation inference inside your network.
06:14 Mark Ellis: Pricing — high level: hosted per-token, dedicated reserved capacity pricing, and private licensing?
06:22 Alex Morales: Exactly. Hosted is usage-based. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with monthly commit pricing. Private is an enterprise license plus support. I'll send a pricing matrix showing rough unit economics for your 150 qps profile.
06:35 Emily Soto: For the POC benchmarks, we want an apples-to-apples comparison with our current OpenAI setup — same prompts, same payloads. Can Redwood replay traffic?
06:45 Liam O'Connor: Yes, we can run a benchmark harness. We'll need samples of typical requests, sequence lengths, and expected concurrency. We'll run dedicated and hosted variants to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
06:58 Ravi Patel: For private deployment, what's the network setup? VPC peering vs private link?
07:05 Priya Shah: We support VPC peering, Private Service Connect on GCP, and on-prem bundles. We'll capture network egress and NAT requirements in the connectivity checklist.
07:18 Mark Ellis: Any caveats with LangChain function calling or tool use? We rely on function-calling for structured outputs to our microservices.
07:27 Priya Shah: Function-calling is supported, including structured output modes and JSON schema hints. Streaming structured output is supported as well, but you should test edge cases in the POC since schema enforcement is at the SDK/app layer.
07:40 Emily Soto: Timeline — we'd like to pilot before end of year. Is that realistic?
07:46 Alex Morales: Yes, if we get mutual NDA and access to sample traffic this week we can schedule the POC for 1-2 weeks, run benchmarks the week after, and present results.
07:56 Mark Ellis: Sounds good. Quick risk check: any limits on simultaneous embeddings jobs? We do nightly batch embeddings for 100k documents.
08:05 Liam O'Connor: For large batch embeddings we recommend using our batch endpoints or running dedicated pools with autoscaling. We can also provide blob import tools to speed up onboarding.
08:18 Priya Shah: Also note that quotas can be bumped for dedicated, and private has no shared tenancy so your throughput is controlled by your reserved capacity.
08:30 Ravi Patel: Ok last question — in the hosted model, are logs multi-tenant visible? We need strict separation.
08:38 Alex Morales: Tenant isolation is maintained; logs are segmented per-tenant. For regulated workloads we still recommend dedicated or private for the cleanest isolation guarantees.
08:50 Emily Soto: Recap and next steps?
08:53 Alex Morales: Recap: Redwood to send pricing/SOC2/connectivity checklist, SE to share LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and demo repo, plan and schedule POC benchmark for dedicated/private. Nova to share sample traffic and SRE constraints. We'll target first POC runs the week of 2026-11-30.
09:11 Mark Ellis: Perfect — thanks everyone, we'll look out for the email.
09:16 Alex Morales: Thanks all, talk soon.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-attribution and automatic caption noise; timestamps approximate. References: demo repo link (shared in follow-up), security pack PDF, pricing spreadsheet (to be sent).
